Subject: Private endpoints — DNS + certs question

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we scope the Private deployment (VPC) option, two immediate questions came up from our security and platform teams around private domains and TLS termination:

1) We plan to expose the private Redwood API at api.redwood.regcorp.internal (internal-only domain). Do you have recommendations on how DNS should be managed (split-horizon Route53 hosted zone vs. forwarding to our internal resolvers)?

2) For certificates: RegCorp runs an internal PKI (Entrust) and requires all services to use certs issued by that CA. Can Redwood support: (a) uploading customer-provided certs, (b) ACME automation against our internal ACME server, or (c) leveraging HashiCorp Vault for signed cert provisioning?

3) TLS termination: we want to understand tradeoffs between terminating TLS at the edge (ALB) vs. end-to-end TLS to the pod/process (mutual TLS). Our compliance team prefers client certs for inter-service auth. Is mTLS supported in Private deployments?

We're trying to finalize a mutual action plan this week. I've attached a rough network drawing. Happy to hop on a call if that helps.

Thanks,
Alice
Alice Kamatel
Head of IT Infrastructure, RegCorp

Hi Alice,

Thanks — this is exactly the kind of detail we need. Looping in Dev (solutions) and Diego (security) to give concrete options. Quick answers up front:

- DNS: split-horizon private hosted zone is usually the simplest for VPC/private endpoints (no public exposure).
- Certs: we support customer-provided certs and automated rotation via integrations (cert-manager with Vault, or ACME against a private CA).
- TLS termination: both edge-termination and E2E (mTLS) are supported; we can recommend based on latency and compliance.

Dev / Diego / Hannah — can you confirm the recommended default architecture and any caveats we should communicate to RegCorp? Also, Alice — can you share your private hosted zone export or the internal resolver details (we can work with a sample).

Next steps: Dev / Diego to give a short pros/cons doc and Marissa will propose a kickoff window.

Subject: Re: Private endpoints — DNS + certs question

Hi Alice — thanks for the diagram. I pulled together a concise set of options below (we'll expand in the call):

Option A — Split-horizon Private Hosted Zone + Edge TLS (recommended default)- DNS: Create a private hosted zone for regcorp.internal in your cloud DNS (Route53 private hosted zone or equivalent). Associate the VPC(s) where Redwood Private runs. This gives single-zone resolution internally without touching public DNS.- TLS: Terminate TLS at the (customer-provided) edge load balancer (ALB/NLB w/ TLS) that sits in front of the Redwood control/data plane. Certs: upload the cert+key (PEM) issued by your CA to the load balancer or use your internal ACME to automate issuance.- Pros: Simplest to operate, works with existing internal PKI, minimal change to Redwood runtime.- Cons: Traffic inside VPC to Redwood backends is plain (unless you opt for TLS passthrough / re-encrypt). Compliance teams sometimes require E2E encryption.

Option B — Split-horizon + Re-encrypt (edge TLS + backend TLS)- DNS: same as A.- TLS: TLS terminated at edge, then re-encrypted from load balancer to Redwood service endpoints using certs signed by your PKI (or mTLS with client certs). You can run cert-manager inside the cluster that fetches certs from Vault / internal ACME.- Pros: Maintains in-transit encryption end-to-end; can enable mTLS for mutual auth.- Cons: More operational work (cert distribution/rotation inside environment).

Option C — TLS Passthrough / SNI routing (E2E TLS to process)- DNS: CNAME or ALIAS pointing directly to the endpoint LB that routes traffic without terminating TLS. The backend presents a cert for api.redwood.regcorp.internal.- Pros: True E2E encryption; simplest from a trust boundary perspective.- Cons: Limits LB routing features (no HTTP path-based routing). Diagnostics (Layer7) are reduced.

Certificates: options we support- Customer-uploaded certs: You can provide PEM cert+key pairs and we will install them on the edge in the Private deployment package.- Private ACME: We support automated issuance against private ACME servers (e.g., Boulder compatible) — cert-manager can be configured with an internal ACME endpoint.- Vault: cert-manager integration with HashiCorp Vault (PKI backend) works well for internal provisioning; for HSM/KMS-backed private CAs we can integrate via Vault or use your signing workflow.

Rotation & Ops- We recommend short rotation windows (90 days or less) and an automated rotation mechanism (cert-manager + Vault or ACME).- For customer-uploaded static certs, we supply a timeline and alerting (30/15/7 days) before expiry and support emergency key swap with a canary cutover.

OCSP/CRL- For internal PKI, OCSP stapling is preferred where supported. If your CA uses CRLs, we need connectivity from our control plane to your CRL/OCSP endpoints for validation checks or a cache gateway in your network.

mTLS- Yes, we support mTLS for the data plane in Private deployments. Typical setup: edge LB performs TLS termination (or not), then backend pods are configured to require client certs issued by your CA. We can use cert-manager + Vault to provision client certs for Redwood sidecars/workers and enforce mutual auth.

Operational recommendations (Hannah/Diego notes):- Use a private hosted zone and avoid split DNS hacks that rely on DNS forwarding unless there is a legacy constraint.- Use SAN entries instead of wildcards for strict compliance auditing when possible.- Store private keys in your KMS/HSM and only allow Redwood to reference certs via an integration (we prefer not to hold private keys long-term).- Provide an IP allowlist and peering/VPN + private hosted zone; avoid exposing management/control endpoints publicly.

Sample minimal deliverables for the kickoff- Private hosted zone export (zone file) or resolver IPs (you mentioned export — please send).- Preferred cert workflow: "customer-upload", "ACME-internal", or "Vault".- Any mandatory compliance requirements: max key lifetime, ciphers, FIPS/HSM requirement.

I'll attach a short export I used to validate routing (private-dns-zone-export.txt). Happy to jump on a call; propose Wed 10am PT for a 30m technical kickoff.

Regards,
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Alice / team — quick security clarifications from my side before the kickoff:

1) Key custody: If RegCorp requires HSM-backed keys, we can integrate via Cloud KMS/HSM or accept references to certificates stored in your HSM and pulled by a cert-proxy inside your VPC. We will not persist private keys in Redwood control plane for Private deployments unless agreed contractually.

2) Cipher suites / TLS profile: We enforce TLS 1.2+ but can restrict cipher suites to match your policy (e.g., FIPS-profile). Provide a policy doc and we'll validate in our acceptance tests.

3) Auditing: We will enable connection-level logs and TLS handshake metadata (SNI, cipher, cert fingerprint) to be sent to your logging endpoint (syslog or our encrypted forwarder). Confirm retention requirement.

4) OCSP/CRL & availability: If OCSP responders are internal-only, ensure our functional subnet has network access (via VPC endpoints or proxy). For high-availability, we recommend deploying an OCSP cache/proxy in your environment.

If this aligns, propose the following immediate tasks for both teams:
- RegCorp: share private hosted zone export and CA policy (key lifetime, required ciphers, HSM requirement).
- Redwood: produce an architecture diagram showing edge termination vs. E2E flows and a short runbook for cert rotation + emergency rotation.

I'll attend the Wed 10am PT call as well.

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
Head of Security, Redwood Inference
